entries.question_en: Where does a BHW's duty come from?
entries.question_fil: Saan nanggagaling ang tungkulin ng isang BHW?
entries.answer_en: It comes from law, not just goodwill: Republic Act 7883, the Barangay Health Workers' Benefits and Incentives Act of 1995, defines the BHW role and the Primary Health Care Approach it follows. A BHW's status becomes official only after training and accreditation by the local health board — being willing to help is not, by itself, enough to begin the work.
entries.answer_fil: Nanggagaling ito sa batas, hindi lang sa kagustuhan: ang Republic Act 7883, ang Barangay Health Workers' Benefits and Incentives Act of 1995, ang nagtatakda ng tungkulin ng BHW at ng Primary Health Care Approach na sinusunod nito. Opisyal na katayuan lamang ang BHW matapos ang pagsasanay at akreditasyon ng local health board — ang pagkagustong tumulong lamang ay hindi sapat para simulan ang gawain.

entries.question_en: Who accredits a BHW before they can officially start their work?
entries.question_fil: Sino ang nagbibigay ng akreditasyon sa isang BHW bago siya opisyal na makapagsimula sa gawain?
entries.answer_en: The local health board, under RA 7883, accredits a BHW after they complete proper training. Neither the midwife nor a fellow BHW has the authority to grant this accreditation on their own — it is a formal step tied to the local health board.
entries.answer_fil: Ang local health board, ayon sa RA 7883, ang nagbibigay ng akreditasyon sa isang BHW matapos ang tamang pagsasanay. Wala ni ang midwife o ang kapwa BHW ng awtoridad na magbigay nito nang mag-isa — pormal na hakbang ito na nakatali sa local health board.

entries.question_en: What benefits can a BHW receive under RA 7883?
entries.question_fil: Anong mga benepisyo ang maaaring matanggap ng isang BHW sa ilalim ng RA 7883?
entries.answer_en: A BHW may be given hazard allowance, subsistence allowance, training/education and career enrichment programs, civil service eligibility, free legal services, and priority access to loans. To be eligible, a BHW must be registered with the local health board of the city or municipality where they serve.
entries.answer_fil: Maaaring bigyan ang BHW ng hazard allowance, subsistence allowance, mga programa sa pagsasanay at career enrichment, civil service eligibility, libreng legal services, at priority access sa mga loan o pautang. Para maging eligible, kailangang rehistrado ang BHW sa local health board ng lungsod o munisipyo kung saan siya nagbibigay ng serbisyo.

entries.question_en: What are the requirements for BHW Eligibility (BHWE) in the Civil Service?
entries.question_fil: Ano ang mga kondisyon para sa BHW Eligibility (BHWE) sa Civil Service?
entries.answer_en: Four conditions: accredited by the local health board, completed a minimum of two years of college, actively and voluntarily serving continuously for five years or more, and having a satisfactory service record as an accredited BHW. A four-year college degree is not required.
entries.answer_fil: Apat na kondisyon: akreditado ng local health board, nakatapos ng minimum na dalawang taon sa kolehiyo, aktibo at boluntaryong naglilingkod nang tuloy-tuloy sa loob ng limang taon o higit pa, at may satisfactory service bilang accredited BHW. Hindi kinakailangan ang four-year college degree.

entries.question_en: What is the local health board responsible for in the accreditation process?
entries.question_fil: Ano ang responsibilidad ng local health board sa proseso ng akreditasyon?
entries.answer_en: Under Section 5 of the RA 7883 IRR, the local health board safeguards the registration and accreditation process, evaluates applications, records its decisions in a board resolution or meeting minutes, issues certificates of registration or accreditation, reviews and approves benefits that use local funds, recommends benefits and fund appropriation, provides an official copy of the BHW registry to the DOH, and monitors the service registered BHWs provide. It may also create a Registration and Accreditation Committee to handle applications.
entries.answer_fil: Ayon sa Section 5 ng RA 7883 IRR, pinangangalagaan ng local health board ang proseso ng rehistrasyon at akreditasyon, sinusuri ang mga aplikasyon, itinatala ang mga desisyon sa board resolution o minutes, naglalabas ng certificate of registration o accreditation, sinusuri at inaaprubahan ang mga benepisyong gagamit ng pondong lokal, nagrerekomenda ng benepisyo at pondo, nagbibigay ng opisyal na kopya ng BHW registry sa DOH, at binabantayan ang serbisyo ng mga rehistradong BHW. Maaari rin itong lumikha ng Registration and Accreditation Committee para sa mga aplikasyon.

entries.question_en: What should a BHW do if their accreditation or benefit is delayed?
entries.question_fil: Ano ang dapat gawin ng BHW kung naantala ang kanyang akreditasyon o benepisyo?
entries.answer_en: Follow up calmly with a specific question — such as the status of the application and whether anything else needs to be submitted — rather than a vague complaint. A clear, calm question is more likely to be answered, and staying silent about a delay often just lets a fixable problem drag on longer.
entries.answer_fil: Mag-follow-up nang kalmado at may tiyak na tanong — tulad ng status ng aplikasyon at kung may kailangan pang ibigay — sa halip na reklamong walang tiyak na hinihingi. Ang malinaw at kalmadong tanong ay mas malamang na masagot, at ang katahimikan sa harap ng pagkaantala ay madalas nagpapahaba lang ng problemang kaya sanang maayos.
